definition.title: Observable Standard Model decays of KK-graviton dark matter

definition.summary: The supplied analysis constrains decay signals and a phenomenological brane-overlap coupling within its tower-evolution model. Naturalness-based mass conclusions require the additional coupling assumption.

assumptions: The 2023 tower mass history and cascade prescription are conditional historical inputs.
The natural-mass interpretation assumes order-one dimensionless decay couplings.
conventions: λ denotes averaged graviton wave-function overlap with the brane.
includes: CMB, IGM heating, diffuse and Galactic photons, and Galactic positrons
excludes: An unconditional present-day dark-matter mass bound

definition.readingLimit: Bounded pages from 2307.11048 support the targets and reported conditional bounds. One source-object evidence item is omitted. The 2026 excerpts challenge the cascade premise; they do not supply a complete reanalysis of these observables.

assessment.note: The excerpts support the listed decay observables and coupling-dependent constraints. The card already marks the 2023 cascade history as conditional and natural-mass conclusions as requiring order-one couplings; later critiques do not supply a complete replacement analysis.

definition.summary: The analysis constrains a velocity combination in a simplified tower model. Its interpretation as Dark Dimension parameter bounds depends on the assumed decay and mass-evolution laws.

assumptions: Approximately equal daughter masses
Last-decay kicks approximate the relevant velocity history
The historical cascade evolution fixes the modeled time dependence
conventions: The principal data constraint is on a velocity combination, not independent measurements of every tower parameter.
includes: Planck CMB, BAO and KiDS-1000 cosmic-shear analysis
excludes: A nonlinear resolution of the σ8 tension
A demonstrated resolution of the Hubble tension
An updated fit using the later threshold law

definition.readingLimit: The supplied version is 2311.05318v1, dated 9 Nov 2023. Its abstract reports a bound, while the supplied body states the approximations. The likelihood, nonlinear evolution and consequences of replacing the cascade law were not checked.

assessment.note: The body explicitly supplies the nonrelativistic, nearly symmetric and last-kick approximations, while the abstract reports the velocity constraint. The card preserves the linear scope of 2311.05318v1, 9 Nov 2023, and makes no nonlinear tension-resolution or updated-fit claim.

Certification of the announced general proof

The admissible cutoff and dimensional matching prescription are contested.
conventions: Separate Λcc from the UV cutoff.
Distinguish a cutoff at mKK from the species-scale cutoff.

excludes: Settling the dispute from introductory excerpts

definition.title: Cosmological survival and depletion of dark relics
definition.question: What controls the cosmological persistence or depletion of proposed dark matter and other relic populations, and which observable consequences test the assumed survival mechanism?
definition.summary: A shared survival target connects charged coherent fields, near-extremal PBHs and KK towers while retaining their different mechanisms. Existing production, radiation and threshold questions remain separately accessible.

systems: Other decaying or annihilating candidates through the existing source-scoped questions
targets: Persistence, collective depletion and cosmologically acceptable instability
Cascade viability and associated radiation constraints
regimes: Finite-time near-extremality and nonextremal merger products
Source-specific early and late cosmological evolution
assumptions: Protection against individual-particle decay does not establish protection against annihilation
Suppressed Hawking emission and suppressed charge loss require separate assessments
A partial decay threshold law does not by itself specify a complete cascade history
A freeze-in population may be constrained even when another component supplies dark matter
conventions: Net-neutral populations are distinct from electrically neutral constituents
Exact extremality and finite-time near-extremality remain distinct
The earlier KK s-wave estimate is a rejected comparator in the supplied 2026 source
Different survival mechanisms are not aliases
includes: Connections to production and signal questions without identifying their targets
excludes: A common stabilization mechanism
Universal exclusions of light bosons, charged PBHs or extra-dimensional models
An updated observational fit inferred solely from a changed decay law

definition.readingLimit: Bounded excerpts support the mechanisms and attributed conclusions, not their complete calculations. The millicharged source is v2 dated 5 May 2021, the near-extremal PBH source is v1 dated 11 June 2019, and the supplied KK source is v1 dated 1 October 2026. Other linked survival questions retain their inherited reading limits.

methods: Threshold partial-wave analysis and conditional cosmological constraints

assessment.note: Cosmological persistence is an explicit shared target across the charged-field, PBH and KK contrasts. The card correctly separates collective annihilation, suppressed evaporation and discharge, and cascade dynamics. Its inclusion of other relic populations accommodates the freeze-in constraint without requiring KK dark matter. Source-reported results remain bounded by the stated reading limits.

Hidden gauge sectors and scalar-coupled cosmologies
Extra-dimensional constructions and their relic populations

includes: Negative viability results and historical hypotheses with their status preserved

definition.readingLimit: Only the supplied contrast descriptions, bounded primary excerpts, exact graph context and attributed child ledgers were assessed. assessment.note: Retain the exact prior scope. The contrasts substantiate a family spanning candidate reviews, thermal histories and distinct survival mechanisms. This supports navigation without independently validating the descendant corpus or admitting c0.
